observations: Torah #120 of LM2 contains no bechina (parallel aspect / shared nature) declarations. The teaching is entirely practical and advisory: it discusses kavvanot in prayer, the danger of practicing them unworthily (compared to kishuf via the drasha 'lo tilmad la'asot'), and the primacy of perush hamilot (simple word-meaning) as the vehicle for devekut. All relationships in this torah are eitza-type (cause-and-effect / practical advice): praying with kavvanot without worthiness LEADS TO something like kishuf; focusing on perush hamilot LEADS TO devekut. Since there are no bechina-connected concepts — neither 3+ concepts forming an independent domain nor any bechina connections at all — no new packages can be proposed.
